hypotheses.claim: Fresh crypto-specific catalysts tilt subsequent XRP moves: upbeat Ripple/XRP headlines (listings, approvals, wins) push up; negative ones (lawsuits, hacks, delistings) push down.
hypotheses.prediction: decisive catalyst reads align with 24h direction more often than chance

hypotheses.claim: The news-catalyst member beats the baseline forecast out-of-sample on Brier score.
hypotheses.prediction: member Brier < baseline Brier over n ≥ 200 scored forecasts

hypotheses.claim: Catalyst effects fade fast: headlines older than a day carry no usable signal, and most decay within hours.
hypotheses.prediction: older catalysts do not improve the read vs recency-weighted ones
hypotheses.test: tilt skill vs catalyst age from lab notes

hypotheses.claim: The catalyst read expresses itself often enough to matter — not a once-a-quarter curiosity.
hypotheses.prediction: decisive_frac ≥ 0.40 over rolling history once n ≥ 100

disciplines_applied.assessment: The wire is mostly quiet (1.1% decisive). A headline is a lead, not a verdict — and I never confuse a rumor for a confirmed event.

Scope discipline: crypto-specific catalysts only (Ripple/XRP/XRPL, listings, regulation, hacks) — the macro calendar already covers scheduled econ events. Relevance triage is keyword-based and labeled as such; polarity can misread tone and I guard it.
decisive_frac=1.1% over n=91; scoreboard still warming up (n=83/200). Catalyst events are rare — I size my claims to my sample.

When in doubt I vote HOLD: adopting noise corrupts every forecast it touches, and that is the costliest error I can make. Timing risk is priced too — the market may have traded the headline before my feed ever saw it.
Pipeline healthy: feeds reachable 96.7% of cycles; every catalyst carries its real headline, source, and timestamp — nothing invented, ever.

Breaking news is usually priced by the time it reaches an RSS reader — the edge in news is measured in minutes, and my feed is slow. That is why no APPLY verdict of mine ever skips out-of-sample proof.
